extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, journalists, newsroom leaders, media stakeholders and media-literacy advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and news about news organizations adopting the Trust Project's standards (the 8 Trust Indicators®) to demonstrate transparency, independence and trustworthy journalism across platforms. Focused on implementing policies, disclosures and visible signals (Trust Mark) that communicate journalistic integrity to audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 Trust Indicators® (journalism transparency standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 8 Trust Indicators® – a “gold standard” in journalism transparency – emphasize the fundamentals of honest journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations work with the Trust Project to implement the 8 Trust Indicators® into journalistic processes; the indicators are integrated into news sites, podcasts, video and print. Earning the Trust Mark indicates that an outlet has incorporated the indicators and is committed to their standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices (rigorous, clear policies and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigorous, clear policies and standards with the commitment to back them up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is described as an anchor Trust Indicator that outlets rolled out after months-long upgrades. Best Practices should be published, enforceable, and visibly backed by newsroom commitment and operational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving the public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize the fundamentals of honest journalism: serving the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage and editorial decisions should prioritize public value and hold power to account, including reporting on solutions to everyday problems and serving voiceless communities, as part of the Trust Indicators' aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separating opinion and paid content from news
rubrics_metrics.description: Separating opinion and paid content from news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms must clearly distinguish news reporting from opinion pieces and paid/promoted content through labeling, placement, and policy so audiences can tell editorial content from sponsored material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting newsgathering from funder influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting newsgathering from funder ... (protecting newsgathering from funder influence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should have safeguards and disclosures to prevent funders or sponsors from influencing reporting. This is listed among the core fundamentals of honest journalism within the Trust Indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified journalism / commitment to independent journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust Project news partners give you verified journalism... commitment to independent journalism of public value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlets adopting the indicators present evidence of verification practices, editorial independence, and institutional commitment to factual, accountable reporting as part of demonstrating trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of transparency elements builds trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic transparency elements are both read by users and significantly strengthen credibility and trust in news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eye-tracking research cited indicates that transparency disclosures and indicators should be made visible and easily discoverable on pages and across platforms because they measurably increase audience trust and credibility judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform integration of Trust Indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: The integrity behind these indicators is now built into El Tiempo’s journalistic processes, news site, podcasts, video and even print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation should not be limited to a website: incorporate policies, disclosures and signals into audio, video, print and other formats so the Trust Indicators apply across an outlet's outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitments to tackle misinformation (continuous education)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pledge consists of ten commitments that focus on investing resources in the continuous education of employees, clients and audiences on information threats and trusted media sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media stakeholders are encouraged to adopt organizational commitments including ongoing training and public education about misinformation and trusted sources as part of a broader trust-building strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earning and displaying the Trust Mark
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations earn the Trust Mark after incorporating the 8 Trust Indicators® into their journalistic processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Mark functions as a visible signal to audiences that an outlet has implemented the indicators; outlets should integrate the mark and accompanying disclosures into their sites and communications to demonstrate accountability.
